voice.subhead: Describe what you ate and the AI will estimate the calories and macros.

voice.tip: Include quantities where you can — "two scoops", "a handful" — and the estimate gets a lot better.

accuracy.exHint: Never all of it: burn estimates run high, and people tend to move less for the rest of a day they trained. Auto goes by your activity level: sedentary adds 40%, lightly active 30%, moderately active 25%, very active nothing (that target already includes your training). Exercise is logged and shown either way.
accuracy.learnHint: After about two weeks of logging and weighing in, SnapCal works out what you really burn from your own data and sets your target from that.
accuracy.cardUsing: Your target is based on this.
accuracy.cardNotYet: Not used yet — needs a bit more data.
accuracy.cardBuilding: Keep logging meals and weighing in. After about two weeks, SnapCal will show what you really burn here.
accuracy.cardHow: Worked out from {days} days of eating (average {intake} kcal) and your weight trend ({rate} kg a week). It includes your exercise, daily movement and logging habits.
accuracy.cardSkipped: {n} days that looked only partly logged were left out.
accuracy.exNoteOff: Logged, not added to today's budget — burn estimates run high. You can change this in Profile.

onb.installTitle: Put SnapCal on your Home Screen
onb.installSub: It opens full screen like an app, loads faster, and on iPhone it's the only way to get notifications.
onb.ios2: Tap ••• next to the address bar, then Share {icon}. On older iPhones, Share is at the bottom of the screen.
onb.ios3: Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen {icon}.

onb.iosNote: In Chrome on iPhone, Share is in the address bar.
onb.android1: In Chrome, tap the menu {icon} at the top right.
onb.android2: Tap Install app or Add to Home screen {icon}.
onb.android3: Tap Install. SnapCal appears with your apps — open it from there.
onb.androidNote: Samsung Internet: tap the menu ☰, then Add page to → Home screen.

members.title: People and groups
members.hint: Tap a group to add or remove someone. People with no group see only themselves. Remove takes someone out of the app for good.
members.removeConfirm: Remove {name} from SnapCal? Their account and everything in it (meals, photos, weight, notes) are deleted, and their phone is signed out. This can't be undone.

redo.hint: Walk through the questions again — useful to switch to pounds and feet, or after a change in build or goal. Your meals, weigh-ins and history are kept.

weekend.aheadBody: Two days that undo four is the most common pattern there is. Log them like any other day and they usually behave.
weekend.saturdayBody: Nothing is off limits today — just log it while you remember. Saturday you log beats Saturday you guess at on Monday.
weekend.sundayBody: One more day. A weekend logged honestly is worth more than a perfect-looking week with two blank days in it.
weekend.withNumber: Over your last {weekends} weekends you've averaged {n} kcal a day more than on weekdays. Not a problem — just worth knowing before Saturday night.
weekend.under: Your weekends actually run {n} kcal a day lighter than your weekdays. Whatever you're doing, keep it.

bf.hipHint: Around the widest part of the hips and glutes.

whatsNew.title: What's new in SnapCal
whatsNew.n1Body: SnapCal can now tell you when someone shares a meal, comments on yours, sends you a note, or your Friday check-in is ready.
whatsNew.n2Body: Turn them on or off anytime in Profile, under Notifications. You only hear about your own groups.

privacy.downloaded: Downloaded. The file has everything stored about you.
privacy.deleteWarn: This permanently deletes your account and everything in it: meals, photos, weight, exercise, notes, shared posts. It can't be undone. Download your data first if you want a copy.
privacy.deleteConfirm: Delete your account and all your data for good?
privacy.deleted: Your account and data have been deleted.
privacy.consentSub: SnapCal keeps health information about you, so we need your OK first. In short:
privacy.point1: We store what you log — meals, photos, weight, exercise and body details — to run the app and sync your phones.
privacy.point2: Meal photos and descriptions are sent to Google's Gemini AI to estimate calories. Google may keep them to improve its products.
privacy.point3: Your group sees your daily totals and whatever you share. Nothing is sold or used for ads.
privacy.point4: Calorie numbers are estimates, not medical advice. You can download or delete everything any time in Profile → Privacy.
privacy.read: Read the full privacy policy & terms
privacy.agree: I'm 16 or older, I've read the privacy policy and terms, and I agree to SnapCal processing my health data as described.
privacy.agreeSignup: I'm 16 or older and I agree to the
privacy.tickFirst: Please tick the box to agree first.
